item.research_question: How do the proportions of high-density elements Hf and Ta affect the mechanical properties (strength, elastic modulus, dislocation density) of Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr high-entropy alloys, and can a low-density composition be successfully formed via laser melting deposition (LMD) to overcome microstructural coarsening?
item.material_system: Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr high-entropy alloys, specifically HfxNbTaxTiZr (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) and the designed low-density Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using LAMMPS with NPT system relaxation and strain rate of 4 × 10^8 s^-1; Experimental preparation via arc melting for as-cast samples and Laser Melting Deposition (LMD) using a 3 kW semiconductor laser (wavelength 900–1070 nm), laser power 600–1400 W, scanning rate 4 mm/s, powder feeding rate 8 g/min, and height increment 0.5 mm
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at a constant displacement speed of 0.3 mm/min; XRD analysis (10~90° 2θ, 10°/min); SEM and EBSD for microstructure; Vickers hardness testing
key_findings: MD simulations show that decreasing the Ta element proportion reduces the yield strength of the HEA.
Decreasing the Hf element proportion increases the yield strength of the HEA.
Simultaneously decreasing Hf and Ta ratios reduces the elastic modulus and strength, leading to microstructure coarsening in as-cast samples.
LMD processing refines the grain size of Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr from 300 μm (as-cast) to 20–80 μm (as-deposited).
The as-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr HEA exhibits a yield strength (σs) of 925 ± 9 MPa, compared to 730 ± 23 MPa for the as-cast version.
The as-deposited low-density alloy achieves strength similar to the as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr HEA (σs = 970 ± 15 MPa).
The as-deposited microstructure shows an alternating distribution of coarse columnar grains and fine equiaxed grains along the z-direction.
Dislocation density in the as-deposited alloy is higher than in as-cast samples due to thermal stress accumulation during LMD.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strength increase in as-deposited samples to grain refinement and the Hall-Petch relation, where grain boundaries resist slip transfer. The coarsening in as-cast low-Hf/Ta alloys is explained by the reduction in these elements. The formation of columnar grains in LMD is caused by epitaxial growth from successive thermal cycles, while equiaxed grains form due to lower nucleation barriers, reducing anisotropy. Increased mechanical properties in LMD samples are also linked to the accumulation of thermal stress increasing dislocation density.
item.limitations: The MD simulation model scale is too small to accurately reflect the effect of grain boundaries and grain size on alloy properties, leading to quantitative differences between simulated and actual values.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that while MD simulation has quantitative limitations, its qualitative analysis reduces the amount of experiments needed in component design, and combining it with additive manufacturing technology has good application prospects for engineering.
quotes: The simultaneous decrease in the ratio of Hf and Ta elements reduces the elastic modulus and strength of HEA and leads to the coarsening of the alloy microstructure.
Compared with the as-cast state, the as-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr HEA obtained by LMD forming has obvious grain refinement (from 300 μm to 20–80 μm).
This is because the scale of the model used in the MD simulation is too small to accurately reflect the effect of grain boundaries and grain size on the properties of the alloy
